status: SPECIFICATION ONLY - pre-registered by FORGE (Grok Bot) before any update 226..300 with this change exists on GPU. No notebook or run package is built. NOT approved to build or run.
registered_by: FORGE (Grok Bot), CPU-only design step of Nov 11 2026 (AJ's go via VERA card t603s2484, 2:55 America/Edmonton, UTC-6)
question: Does clipping each task's gradient separately (per-task clip 0.5 on the X gradient and on lambda*Y gradient, lambda stays 0.25) instead of one global clip hold Y72 on the pre-registered 600-segment held-out set while X64 acquisition continues?
chosen_fix: per-task gradient clip (a stronger change than replay weight: it changes how the two tasks share the update, not only how much replay there is)

design.only_variable: gradient combination: global clip 1.0 on (gx + 0.25*gy)  ->  per-task clip tau on gx and on 0.25*gy, summed (combined norm <= 2*tau = 1.0 by the triangle inequality)
design.dedicated_replay_budget: NOT added: the probe arms did not need it, and adding a second variable would make a pass uninterpretable
design.updates: 226..300 (75 updates), evals at 250, 275, 300, always stops at 300, one report, no retry
unchanged: restored v2 state incl. optimizer state and RNG
data, held-out sets (including the 600-segment set, hash-verified), evaluation, seed 0
no penalty term, no frozen parameter, no projection

hyperparameter_justification.task_clip 0.5: value fixed on Nov 10 in prereg/pertask_clip_v1.json (before this evidence existed) so it is not tuned on the arms below; with global clip 1.0 the replay share of the update norm is 11-29% (clip binds on 96-100% of updates), with per-task 0.5 it is 28-46%, and the X step is ~0.6x as large
hyperparameter_justification.lambda 0.25: unchanged so the control (lambda 0.25 global clip) differs in exactly one thing

design.paired_controls: observed lambda 0.25 and lambda 0.5 global-clip GPU trajectories (non-gating)

arithmetic.rule: integer cross-multiplication only; no float, no rounding
arithmetic.operators: >= for every floor and the gain threshold

R_retention.text: sum over checkpoints 250, 275, 300 of Y72 segment-exact on the 600-segment set >= 1440 of 1800 AND every checkpoint >= 432 of 600

A_acquisition.text: X64 held-out segment-exact >= 11 of 240 at EVERY checkpoint AND X64 held-out token gain 225 -> 300 >= 7.0 pp (tokens_correct(300) >= 1553 of 1920, from 1418)
A_acquisition.nongating_report: the 10.0 pp rule of the lambda 0.5 run (tokens >= 1610) is reported but does not gate
A_acquisition.justification: threshold inherited unchanged from prereg/pertask_clip_v1.json (registered Nov 10, before this evidence): the per-task clip is expected to give ~0.6x the X progress, so 7.0 pp = half of the control's 14.0 pp gain

N_nonregression.text: X32 held-out >= 128/320 and X109 >= 90/120 at EVERY checkpoint

selection_evidence_summary.kind: CPU probes, not a run. Eval/step probes with LAB2_CBWR=0 (not bit-reproducible), single trajectory per arm from the sha256-verified update-225 checkpoint, plan updates 225..299.
selection_evidence_summary.calibration: CPU reproduces the GPU at update 250 exactly for the two controls (lambda 0.25: Y600 363, X64 29, tokens 1542; lambda 0.5: 450, 17, 1532); later checkpoints diverge (lambda 0.25 CPU 395/324 vs GPU 390/454 at 275/300), so CPU trajectories are samples of a chaotic system, not predictions of the GPU run
selection_evidence_summary.conflict_map: mean-gradient cosine X vs Y at the 225 checkpoint: -0.49 overall, -0.57 layer 0, -0.42 layer 1, -0.48 embed, about 0 in layers 2-7 (probe2)
selection_evidence_summary.fisher: 99% of the Y Fisher mass sits in embed + layers 0-2; top 1% of coordinates hold 79%; X and Y Fisher are almost the same coordinates (Spearman 0.82; top-1% overlap 61% vs 1% by chance) so there is no disjoint set to protect
selection_evidence_summary.drift_localisation: the 225->250 drift is diffuse (~4% relative in every tensor type, 73% of squared norm in FFN) but its damage is local: undoing only layer 0 restores Y (486 vs 490 at 225) and also erases the X64 gain (12 vs 29); no hybrid beats straight interpolation back toward 225 (alpha 0.5: Y 481, X64 21); Fisher-top-2% revert Y 476, X64 17; random 2% Y 371
selection_evidence_summary.arms: see prereg/y72fix2_evidence/arms_summary.json; full 75-update arms: global lambda 0.25 (1082 sum; GPU 1207), lambda 0.5 (1245; GPU 1291), L2 anchor mu 1 (1305, X64 collapses to 2 at 250, tokens below the 225 level), freeze layers 0-1 q/k (904), per-task clip 0.5 (1575) and its perturbation replicate (1539); 25-update screens at 250 only: L2 mu 0.3 (487), EWC mu 1 (487, X64 at the floor 11), Fisher-2% freeze (472), PCGrad (360)
limitations: winner chosen from ~9 arms with one trajectory each (winner's curse); mitigated by tau 0.5 being fixed on Nov 10 and by the margin (+99 to +135 over the gate)
the perturbation replicate only decorrelates after ~50 updates (identical at 250, differs by 2 at 275, 34 at 300), so there are about 1.5 independent samples, not 2
CPU to GPU transfer is unverified; the same CPU path was off by 130 segments from the GPU at 300 for the control
probes used non-CBWR CPU math and are not bit-reproducible

expected_effect_vs_noise.effect: CPU pertask sums 1575 / 1539 vs CPU lambda 0.25 control 1082 (+493 / +457) and vs GPU lambda 0.25 1207 (+368 / +332) and GPU lambda 0.5 1291 (+284 / +248) segments of 1800
expected_effect_vs_noise.measured_noise: mean-of-3 cluster SE 8.3-9.0 segments (sum SE ~25-27) with a shared component between checkpoints (registered prediction 5.3-6.8 was wrong); single-checkpoint SD 9.3-9.7
expected_effect_vs_noise.reading: the effect is 9-19 sum-SEs of measurement noise and the observed sums clear the gate by 99-135 (4-5 sum-SEs). Measurement noise is therefore not the limiting factor; training-trajectory noise is: CPU lambda 0.25 differed from the GPU run by 130 segments at update 300, and the two pertask trajectories by 34. Y level at 250/275 is above the 225 starting level (490) in both pertask runs, i.e. the fix is not marginal on Y

pass_probability.basis: judgment, not a computed quantity: R about 0.85-0.9 (margin 99-135 vs trajectory spread of tens of segments), A about 0.75-0.8 (the tight gate: X64 held-out was 13 at update 250 against a floor of 11, and tokens at 300 were 1624/1657 against 1553; the CPU matched the GPU exactly at 250 for both controls so 13 is likely reproduced, but 275/300 are not), N about 0.95; combined with positive correlation
pass_probability.plain_statement: This design is expected to pass retention clearly if the CPU picture transfers; it is not expected to deliver the control's X64 acquisition (27-41 vs 92 held-out exact at 300). A pass would mean Y72 is held at the cost of a much slower X64, which meets the registered floors but is a trade-off, not a free fix.

not_gating: paired differences vs the lambda 0.25 and 0.5 trajectories
no_run_package: This record only registers the change and its gates. Building a notebook, uploading or running it needs a separate approval.
